question: An electric car advert, worded the way many are. Where do the car's emissions actually go?
answer: Up the power line. Norway's electricity is almost all hydropower, at a few tens of grams of carbon dioxide per kilowatt-hour; Poland's leans on coal, at over 600. A car using 0.18 kWh a kilometre emits about 108 grams per km in Poland, close to a frugal petrol car, and a few in Norway.
move: Ask what powers a thing, not just what it is called.
ask: Which of my choices looks clean but depends on something upstream I never see?

scene.head: Car advert
scene.title: Drive electric
scene.body: Zero emissions. 100% electric, 0 g CO2/km. Charge at home and drive clean.

phrases.why: Nothing leaves a tailpipe because there isn't one. The power station is another matter.

phrases.plain: 0 g at the car, about 108 g/km on a coal grid
phrases.why: At 0.18 kWh per km and 600 g per kWh. On Norway's hydropower, a few grams.

phrases.plain: drive as clean as your grid
phrases.why: The car runs on whatever the local power stations burn.

scene.ask: One number depends on a country the advert never names. Which?
scene.watch: For anything electric, ask what the local power stations burn.
